fullPassage:
Humanitas is a yellow brick house located in the city of Deventer, the Netherlands. It is a care center that houses more than 160 elderly residents who require assistance. Along with its supportive environment, Humanitas offers something unusual: young neighbors. At Humanitas, elderly residents share their living space with university students.

This unique "intergenerational living" project began in 2012, after budget cuts reduced the amount of money care homes in the Netherlands received. This funding reduction led to the loss of many essential elderly care programs, including social, educational, and counseling services.

Humanitas needed to seek an affordable solution to fill the gap left by the removal of these services. Since the building had numerous empty rooms available, the director decided to offer local university students free accommodations in return for spending time with the elderly residents. Many students were struggling to afford the area's high rents, so the proposal was a true win-win situation. Now, let's hear more about this intriguing place from two of the residents.

Hi! My name is Jacob Jansen, and I've been living at Humanitas for over two years. I've really enjoyed my time here. As a live-in student, I'm required to spend at least 30 hours per month with my elderly neighbors in exchange for free accommodations. In reality, however, we spend a lot more time together than that. Sometimes I teach them things, such as how to use social media, and other times I just hang out with them. We have meals together, play games, and go shopping.

Humanitas doesn't feel like a care home to me. Instead, I consider it a community that I am a part of. Every time I come home, I tell my neighbors about my day. When I have a problem, they always have useful advice to share. With so much experience gathered over a lifetime, they possess knowledge that I have yet to acquire. They also teach me lots of little but important things, often without realizing it. For example, I've learned the value of having a casual chat over a cup of coffee from them. It's a really great way to take a break from rushing around all the time.

I used to feel sorry for the elderly because I focused only on the things they can't do. When I look at them now, however, I see all the things they can do. Obviously, Humanitas provides me with much more than a free place to stay. I've made deep, meaningful friendships that I'll never forget here.

I intend to stay at Humanitas for at least one more year. Living here has changed my life in ways I never thought possible, and I'm really grateful for this transformative experience. I have learned so much from my neighbors already, but I'm sure there is still a lot more that they can teach me.

My name is Helena Smit, and I am 93 years old. I have been living at Humanitas for the past 15 years, so I remember when we were first informed that we would have young people as neighbors. Believe me, not everyone was happy about it! But that quickly changed once they moved in. The students here are energetic, friendly, and caring. They make us laugh and create a joyful mood.

Humanitas was already a decent place to live before the students arrived, but it has become a lot more fun since they moved in. Recently, the students held a pajama party and invited us to join them. They taught us how to play some new games, and we all had a great time. It was like we were in our 20s again.

I sometimes hear loud music from my young next-door neighbor's apartment, but that is okay. It's a small matter compared to what they've brought to our lives. I'm grateful every day that they have become part of our community.

Speaking of my young neighbor, she has been here for more than two years now. Last year, she went through a difficult time of grief after she lost her father, so I did what came naturally. I stayed with her, held her hands when she cried, and listened to what she said. She later told me that I was a great comfort during that difficult time, which made me feel very good. It always feels nice to be reminded that I'm still capable of doing things for others.

I am nearly 100 years old, and I have bad knees. I understand that my knees aren't going to get any better. There is nothing much the doctors can do about the pain. But having young, vibrant people around helps me forget about the pain and enjoy my life!

There are currently six students living at Humanitas, with a long waiting list of others hoping to be offered a spot. Humanitas is a great example of how people of different ages can help each other and share their lives with one another. The older residents gain a more youthful perspective on life, while the younger residents receive valuable life lessons. More and more care homes around Europe are now trying intergenerational living, bringing the young and old together in harmony.

questions.passage: Humanitas is a yellow brick house located in the city of Deventer, the Netherlands. It is a care center that houses more than 160 elderly residents who require (A)[assistance / independence]. Along with its supportive environment, Humanitas offers something (B)[unusual / ordinary]: young neighbors. At Humanitas, elderly residents share their living space with university students. This unique "intergenerational living" project began in 2012, after budget cuts (C)[reduced / increased] the amount of money care homes received.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 도움이 필요한(require assistance) 노인 거주자를 수용하고, 특이한(unusual) 요소인 젊은 이웃을 제공하며, 예산 삭감으로 돈이 줄어들었다(reduced).
det.analysis:
✅ ① assistance — unusual — reduced: 원문 일치
❌ ② independence(독립): 도움이 필요한 노인이므로 부적절
❌ ③ ordinary(평범한): '젊은 이웃'이라는 요소가 특이한 것
❌ ④ increased(증가한): 예산 삭감으로 줄어들었으므로 반대
det.tip: assistance(도움) ↔ independence(독립). unusual(특이한) ↔ ordinary(평범한). reduced(줄어든) ↔ increased(증가한).

questions.passage: This unique "intergenerational living" project began in 2012, after budget cuts reduced the amount of money care homes in the Netherlands received. This funding reduction led to the loss of many essential elderly care programs, including social, educational, and counseling services. Humanitas needed to seek an (A)[affordable / expensive] solution to fill the gap left by the removal of these services. Since the building had (B)[numerous / few] empty rooms available, the director decided to offer local university students free accommodations in return for spending time with the elderly residents. Many students were struggling to afford the area's high rents, so the proposal was a true (C)[win-win / lose-lose] situation. Now, let's hear more about this intriguing place from two of the residents.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 저렴한(affordable) 해결책을 찾아야 했고, 많은(numerous) 빈방이 있어서, 그 제안은 모두에게 유리한(win-win) 상황이었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ affordable — numerous — win-win: 원문 일치
❌ ① few(적은): numerous의 반의어. 빈방이 적으면 학생 수용 불가
❌ ② expensive(비싼): affordable의 반의어. 예산 삭감 상황에서 비싼 해결책은 부적절

det.tip: affordable(저렴한) ↔ expensive(비싼). numerous(많은) ↔ few(적은). win-win(상생) ↔ lose-lose(공멸).

questions.passage: With so much experience gathered over a lifetime, they possess knowledge that I have yet to (A)[acquire / forget]. questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: 그분들은 내가 아직 얻지 못한(acquire) 지식을 가지고 있고, 의미 있는(meaningful) 우정을 쌓았으며, 이 변화의 경험에 감사한다(grateful).
det.analysis:
✅ ② acquire — meaningful — grateful: 원문 일치
❌ ① superficial(피상적인): meaningful의 반의어. 'deep' + 'never forget'과 모순
❌ ③ forget(잊다): acquire의 반의어. '아직 얻지 못한 지식'이 맞음

det.tip: acquire(얻다) ↔ forget(잊다). meaningful(의미 있는) ↔ superficial(피상적인). grateful(감사한) ↔ indifferent(무관심한). 'yet to acquire' = 아직 얻지 못한.

det.analysis:
✅ ① youthful(젊은): 원문 일치
✅ ② valuable(소중한): 원문 일치

✅ ④ caring(배려하는): 원문 일치

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중에서 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ④ 원문은 'without realizing it(모르는 사이에)'인데, 'without intending it(의도하지 않고)'으로 바뀌었다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① community(공동체): 원문 일치
✅ ② useful(유용한): 원문 일치
✅ ③ acquire(얻다): 원문 일치
❌ ④ intending(의도하다) → realizing(깨닫다): 원문은 '깨닫지 못한 채' 가르쳐 준다는 뜻. 'intending'은 유사하지만 원문과 다름
det.tip: without realizing it(모르는 사이에) ≠ without intending it(의도하지 않고). 미묘한 차이: realizing은 인식, intending은 의도. 원문은 realizing.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

✅ ④ win-win(상생): 학생(무료 거처) + 노인(함께할 이웃) 양쪽 모두 이득
❌ ① lose-lose(공멸): 양쪽 모두 이득이므로 반대

det.korean: 깊고 의미 있는(meaningful) 우정을 쌓았다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ trivial(사소한): meaningful의 반의어
❌ ① significant(중요한): meaningful의 동의어 — 함정
❌ ② profound(깊은): meaningful의 동의어 — 함정
❌ ④ important(중요한): meaningful의 동의어 — 함정
det.tip: meaningful = significant = profound = important (의미 있는). 반의어: trivial(사소한), meaningless(무의미한). 동의어 3개 함정 고난도.

questions.passage:
(A) It is a care center that <u>houses</u> more than 160 elderly residents who require assistance.

(B) The word <u>houses</u> can also carry a different meaning depending on context.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 두 단어(houses / homes)의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: (A) 160명 이상의 노인을 수용하는(houses) 요양 시설. (B) 유럽의 요양 시설들(homes)이 세대 간 생활을 시도.
det.analysis:
✅ ② (A) 수용하다 — (B) 시설/요양원: houses는 동사(수용하다), homes는 명사(care homes = 요양 시설)
❌ ① (A) 집들: 여기서 houses는 동사
❌ ③ (B) 집들: care homes = 요양 시설이지 단순 '집'이 아님
❌ ④ (A) 집들: houses가 동사 자리에 있음
det.tip: house: ① 명사 — 집 ② 동사 — 수용하다. home: ① 명사 — 집/가정 ② care home — 요양 시설. 문맥에서 품사를 파악해야 함.

questions.stem:
다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어를 고르시오.

"a place where someone lives; a room or building provided for someone to stay in"

det.korean: "누군가가 사는 곳; 머무를 수 있도록 제공된 방이나 건물" → 거처(accommodation)
det.analysis:
✅ ④ accommodation(거처/숙소): 정의와 정확히 일치
❌ ① assistance(도움): 물리적 공간이 아님
❌ ② counseling(상담): 서비스의 종류
❌ ③ perspective(관점): 추상적 개념
det.tip: accommodation(숙소/거처): accommodate(수용하다)의 명사형. 본문에서 'free accommodations'로 사용.

questions.passage: This funding reduction led to the loss of many essential elderly care programs. Humanitas needed to seek an affordable solution to fill the gap left by the __________ (remove) of these services.
questions.stem: 다음 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (1단어) (영어로) (   ) 쓰시오.

det.korean: 이 서비스들의 제거(removal)로 남은 공백을 메우기 위해.
det.analysis: ✅ removal: remove(동사) → removal(명사). the + _____ + of 구조에서 명사 필요.
det.tip: remove(제거하다) → removal(제거). -al 접미사로 동사→명사 변환. the removal of ~ = ~의 제거.

questions.passage: I've made deep, meaningful friendships that I'll never forget here. Living here has changed my life in ways I never thought possible, and I'm really __________ (gratitude) for this transformative experience. I have learned so much from my neighbors already.
questions.stem: 다음 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 (1단어) (영어로) (   ) 쓰시오.

det.korean: 이 변화의 경험에 정말 감사한(grateful).
det.analysis: ✅ grateful: gratitude(명사) → grateful(형용사). be + 형용사 구조에서 형용사 필요.
det.tip: gratitude(감사, 명사) → grateful(감사하는, 형용사). I'm really grateful = 정말 감사하다.

questions.passage:
Humanitas is a yellow brick house located in the city of Deventer, the Netherlands. It is a care center that houses more than 160 elderly residents who require assistance. Along with its supportive environment, Humanitas offers something unusual: young neighbors. At Humanitas, elderly residents share their living space with university students.

This unique "intergenerational living" project began in 2012, after budget cuts reduced the amount of money care homes in the Netherlands received. This funding reduction led to the loss of many essential elderly care programs, including social, educational, and counseling services.

Humanitas needed to seek an affordable solution to fill the gap left by the removal of these services. Since the building had numerous empty rooms available, the director decided to offer local university students free accommodations in return for spending time with the elderly residents. Many students were struggling to afford the area's high rents, so the proposal was a true win-win situation. Now, let's hear more about this intriguing place from two of the residents.

Hi! My name is Jacob Jansen, and I've been living at Humanitas for over two years. I've really enjoyed my time here. As a live-in student, I'm required to spend at least 30 hours per month with my elderly neighbors in exchange for free accommodations. In reality, however, we spend a lot more time together than that. Sometimes I teach them things, such as how to use social media, and other times I just hang out with them. We have meals together, play games, and go shopping.

Humanitas doesn't feel like a care home to me. Instead, I consider it a community that I am a part of. Every time I come home, I tell my neighbors about my day. When I have a problem, they always have useful advice to share. With so much experience gathered over a lifetime, they possess knowledge that I have yet to acquire. They also teach me lots of little but important things, often without realizing it. For example, I've learned the value of having a casual chat over a cup of coffee from them. It's a really great way to take a break from rushing around all the time.

I used to feel sorry for the elderly because I focused only on the things they can't do. When I look at them now, however, I see all the things they can do. Obviously, Humanitas provides me with much more than a free place to stay. I've made deep, meaningful friendships that I'll never forget here.

I intend to stay at Humanitas for at least one more year. Living here has changed my life in ways I never thought possible, and I'm really grateful for this transformative experience. I have learned so much from my neighbors already, but I'm sure there is still a lot more that they can teach me.

My name is Helena Smit, and I am 93 years old. I have been living at Humanitas for the past 15 years, so I remember when we were first informed that we would have young people as neighbors. Believe me, not everyone was happy about it! But that quickly changed once they moved in. The students here are energetic, friendly, and caring. They make us laugh and create a joyful mood.

Humanitas was already a decent place to live before the students arrived, but it has become a lot more fun since they moved in. Recently, the students held a pajama party and invited us to join them. They taught us how to play some new games, and we all had a great time. It was like we were in our 20s again.

I sometimes hear loud music from my young next-door neighbor's apartment, but that is okay. It's a small matter compared to what they've brought to our lives. I'm grateful every day that they have become part of our community.

Speaking of my young neighbor, she has been here for more than two years now. Last year, she went through a difficult time of grief after she lost her father, so I did what came naturally. I stayed with her, held her hands when she cried, and listened to what she said. She later told me that I was a great comfort during that difficult time, which made me feel very good. It always feels nice to be reminded that ____.

I am nearly 100 years old, and I have bad knees. I understand that my knees aren't going to get any better. There is nothing much the doctors can do about the pain. But having young, vibrant people around helps me forget about the pain and enjoy my life!

There are currently six students living at Humanitas, with a long waiting list of others hoping to be offered a spot. Humanitas is a great example of how people of different ages can help each other and share their lives with one another. The older residents gain a more youthful perspective on life, while the younger residents receive valuable life lessons. More and more care homes around Europe are now trying intergenerational living, bringing the young and old together in harmony.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?
ch: I'm still capable of doing things for others
I need more medical attention for my knees
the students should leave Humanitas soon
loud music is the biggest problem at Humanitas

det.korean: 내가 아직 다른 사람을 위해 무언가 할 수 있다는 것이 생각날 때 기분이 좋다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 'capable of doing things for others': 원문 일치. 93세인 Helena가 젊은 이웃에게 위로가 될 수 있다는 보람
❌ ② 의료 관심은 이 문맥의 주제가 아님
❌ ③ 학생들이 떠나야 한다는 내용 없음 (오히려 감사)
❌ ④ 큰 음악 소리는 '사소한 문제(small matter)'라고 했음
det.tip: 'capable of doing things for others' = 남을 위해 할 수 있다는 자부심. Helena의 핵심 감정.

ch: a place where I work as a caregiver
a temporary shelter with strict rules
a community that I am a part of
